draft.title: The postwar settlement
card: The peace treaties of 1919 to 1920 ended World War I. The Treaty of Versailles dealt with Germany. Other treaties dealt with Austria, Hungary, Bulgaria and the Ottoman Empire.
The treaties redrew Europe's borders. Empires such as Austria-Hungary broke up, and new or enlarged states appeared, including Poland and Czechoslovakia.
Germany lost land and had to accept blame for the war and pay reparations. Hungary lost large areas, and millions of Hungarians ended up living outside its new borders.
Italy had been an Allied winner but felt cheated, because it did not receive all the land it had hoped for. Resentment in these countries gave nationalist leaders a grievance to use.
draft.remember: The treaties changed the map, and the terms left many people bitter.

a.q: Why did many Germans and Hungarians resent the postwar treaties?
opts: The terms cost them land and were seen as harsh
The treaties let other states take over their governments
The treaties broke up their countries into small states
The terms made them join a new alliance against their will
a.why: Germany and Hungary lost territory, and Germany also had to accept blame and pay reparations. This made the terms seem harsh and unfair to many people. The treaties did not take over their governments or force them into an alliance.
a.clue: Think about what each country lost under the terms.

b.q: Italy was on the winning side in World War I. Why was it still resentful of the peace settlement?
opts: It did not receive all the land it had hoped for
It was forced to pay reparations to Germany
It lost its empire to the new state of Poland
It was blamed for starting the war in 1914
b.why: Italy had hoped to gain more territory and felt cheated when it did not. Being on the winning side did not stop that resentment. Blame and reparations were put on Germany, not Italy.
b.clue: Winning a war does not mean getting everything you wanted.

a.best: The terms cost them land and were seen as harsh

b.best: It did not receive all the land it had hoped for
